title: Colours of Language
text:
Colour words appear in many idioms that do not describe colour at all. To be green with envy means to feel jealous, while blue blood refers to nobility. These expressions reflect old beliefs about the body and social rank, and they persist even after the beliefs have faded from common knowledge.

Sometimes a popular explanation takes hold quickly. Blue blood is often said to come from Spanish nobles whose skin looked pale, letting their veins show. Linguists doubt this story, since the phrase appears in other languages with different origins. The attraction of a vivid explanation can outweigh the evidence against it.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what does 'to be green with envy' mean?
According to paragraph two, what does a popular explanation say about blue blood?
options: It comes from pale skin and visible veins among Spanish nobles
It comes from a royal recipe
It comes from a sea voyage
It comes from a medical textbook

questions.text: What can be inferred about the Spanish explanation for blue blood?
options: It is supported by all linguists

questions.text: What does the writer suggest about vivid explanations?
options: Their appeal can outweigh the evidence against them
They are useful only to children

vocabulary.definition: a feeling of wanting what someone else has
people of high social rank by birth
producing strong and clear images in the mind

paragraph_translations: ብዙ ሀረጎች የቀለም ቃላትን ይይዛሉ፤ ሆኖም ቀለምን ፈጽሞ አይገልጹም። to be green with envy ማለት መቅናት ሲሆን blue blood ደግሞ መኳንንትነትን ያመለክታል። እነዚህ አገላለጾች ስለ ሰውነትና ማኅበራዊ ደረጃ የቆዩ እምነቶችን ያንጸባርቃሉ፤ እምነቶቹ ከዕውቀት ከደበዘዙ በኋላም ይቀጥላሉ።

አንዳንድ ጊዜ ታዋቂ ማብራሪያ በፍጥነት ይይዛል። blue blood የመጣው ቆዳቸው ገርጥቶ ደም ሥሮቻቸው በሚታዩ የስፔን መኳንንት ነው ይባላል። ቋንቋ ሊቃውንት ይህንን ታሪክ ይጠራጠራሉ፤ ምክንያቱም ሀረጉ በሌሎች ቋንቋዎች የተለያየ አመጣጥ ያለው ሆኖ ይታያል። ግልጽ የሆነ ማብራሪያ መማረክ ከሱ ጋር የሚቃረነውን ማስረጃ ሊያሸንፍ ይችላል።
